subject: Operations
title: Upstream vs. Downstream
description: A quick, practical guide to Upstream vs. Downstream.

hook.text: Upstream is where things are made. Downstream is where they're sold. Mess up either direction and the chain breaks.

buildup.text: Upstream includes raw material suppliers and component makers. Downstream covers distributors, retailers, and customers.

discovery.text: Problems upstream—like a factory fire—cause stockouts downstream. Weak sales downstream ripple up as excess inventory.

twist.text: Most companies focus on their immediate neighbors and ignore partners two or three tiers away. That blind spot hurts.

climax.text: Toyota maps its supply chain four tiers deep. When a sub-tier supplier had a fire, Toyota recovered in days, not months.

punchline.text: Know your chain upstream and downstream—deeply.

quiz.question: What is upstream in a supply chain?
